parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.lead:
Electrons are moving in a vacuum with speed 1.7 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹. The electrons enter a uniform magnetic field of flux density 4.8mT. Fig. 6.1 shows the path of the electrons.

[[fig:f1]]

The path of the electrons remains in the plane of the page.
parts.text: State the direction of the magnetic field.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Show that the magnitude of the force exerted on each electron by the magnetic field is 1.3 × 10⁻¹⁴ N.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: On Fig. 6.1, draw an arrow to indicate the direction of the centripetal acceleration of the electron where it enters the magnetic field at point X.

parts.label: (b)(iv)
parts.text: Use the information in (b)(ii) to calculate the distance *d* between the path of the electrons entering the magnetic field and the path of the electrons leaving it.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
The electrons in (b) are replaced with positrons that are moving with speed 3.4 × 10⁷ m s⁻¹ along the same initial path as the electrons. The positrons enter the magnetic field at point X on Fig. 6.1.

On Fig. 6.1, draw a line to show the path of the positrons through the magnetic field.

figures.caption: Fig. 6.1
figures.alt: A diagram shows electrons entering a shaded magnetic field at point X, following a curved path, and leaving along a path below their entry path; the separation is labelled d.
